option_relations.rationale: Necrotizing fasciitis is a severe bacterial infection of the fascia, not directly related to the provided leaf which specifies septic emboli from Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia.

The option 'Septic emboli with skin necrosis' is directly equivalent to the provided leaf 'Septic emboli (Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia)' as the bacteremia is the source of the septic emboli leading to necrosis.
Necrotizing cellulitis is a severe infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue, distinct from septic emboli causing necrosis.
Pressure necrosis is caused by prolonged pressure on tissue, which is not directly related to the provided leaf of septic emboli from bacteremia.
